record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as segment visibility graphs of finite collections of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Characterize the segment visibility graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \{s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n\}$ be a finite collection of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. The segment visibility graph $G(S)$ is the simple undirected graph whose vertex set is the set of $2n$ endpoints of the segments in $S$, and in which two distinct endpoints $u$ and $v$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open line segment $uv$ does not intersect any segment of $S$ (the segments of $S$ themselves are treated as opaque obstacles, but visibility along a segment of $S$ between its two endpoints is allowed, so each $s_i$ contributes its own edge).

Give a complete combinatorial characterization of the class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ such that $G \in \mathcal{G}$ if and only if there exists a finite collection $S$ of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane with $G \cong G(S)$. Equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on a finite simple graph $G$ for it to be realizable as the segment visibility graph of some finite set of pairwise disjoint line segments in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing segment visibility graphs is widely cited as an unsolved problem in computational and combinatorial geometry. Partial results exist: planar segment visibility graphs have been characterized (as those segment visibility graphs without a $K_5$ minor) and can be recognized in polynomial time, but no full combinatorial characterization of the entire class is known.

status_evidence.title: Planar segment visibility graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes planar segment visibility graphs via excluded K5 minor and gives a polynomial recognition algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: The planar subcase has been characterized, but the general characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved problems in visibility graphs of points, segments, and polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on visibility graphs including the characterization of segment visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization of segment visibility graphs is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Visibility Graphs and k-link Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems page maintained by D. West discussing characterization of visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The general visibility graph characterization remains open.
